title: "They will look to me whom they have pierced" and the great mourning (Zech 12:10–14)
speaker: The LORD (through the prophet)
description: The LORD pours on David's house and Jerusalem a spirit of grace and supplication; they look to "me whom they have pierced" and mourn for him as for an only son; the mourning is like that of Hadad-rimmon in the valley of Megiddo, every clan apart and their wives apart.
in_text_interpretation: The text shifts from "me" to "him"; the pierced one is not named.

interpretations.label: Fulfilled first at the crucifixion of Jesus (John 19:37), completed when Israel turns to him
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: the shift from "me" to "him" shows one essentially one with the LORD yet personally distinct — the Angel of the LORD incarnate (Keil); John cites the verse of the spear-thrust. Objection: Mitchell argues the piercing lies in the past relative to the writer, so it cannot be the future Messiah.

interpretations.label: A past martyr or martyrs (perhaps read through the Servant of Isa 53)
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: the outpouring is future but the piercing already happened; no known individual fits (Zechariah son of Jehoiada, Uriah, Gedaliah are too remote); perhaps godly persons killed late in the Persian period, or the Servant of Isaiah taken as a historical martyr — as later Jews spoke of "Messiah son of Joseph".
